summary: A Gestaldt Consulting Group article, published August 29, 2023 on LinkedIn, argues that Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are central to driving business growth. It explains why KPIs matter for strategy and accountability, outlines common KPI types (financial, sales and marketing, customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, employee performance), and describes SMART goal setting, how to select KPIs, how to measure and track them, and how to use them for data-driven growth decisions. The page's login prompts, navigation and footer boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: Gestaldt Consulting Group's 2023 LinkedIn article explaining how KPIs support business strategy, SMART goals, KPI selection, tracking, and growth decisions.
key_facts: The article 'Driving Growth: The Role of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in Business Strategy' was published by Gestaldt Consulting Group on Aug 29, 2023.
The article describes KPIs as quantifiable metrics that enable businesses to measure their performance and progress towards their goals.
The article states that KPIs are the backbone of a successful business strategy.
Financial KPIs examples include revenue growth rate, profit margin, return on investment (ROI), and cash flow.
Sales and Marketing KPIs examples include lead conversion rate, customer acquisition cost (CAC), customer lifetime value (CLTV), and website traffic.
Customer Satisfaction KPIs examples include Net Promoter Score (NPS), customer retention rate, customer churn rate, and customer satisfaction index (CSI).
Operational Efficiency KPIs examples include production cycle time, order fulfillment time, inventory turnover rate, and employee productivity.
Employee Performance KPIs examples include employee turnover rate, employee satisfaction index, employee engagement score, and training completion rate.
SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound.
The article's example of a specific goal is 'increase sales by 15% in the next quarter'.
The article advises choosing actionable KPIs and avoiding vanity metrics that do not provide actionable insights.
The article recommends that businesses define clear metrics, set benchmarks and targets, collect and analyse data, monitor and report regularly, and take corrective actions.
The article says that KPI selection is not a one-time exercise and should be reviewed as business goals change.
The article's example of using KPIs for growth is noticing a sudden increase in website traffic and exploring ways to convert visitors into customers.
The article states that the KPI process helps create a culture of accountability and transparency.
